meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-25 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 mins | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (BlueRidge ML), Ethan Marsh (BlueRidge Platform), Sofia Alvarez (BlueRidge Security)
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize console qprofile presets for INT8 and FP8. Live demo comparing latency/fidelity across sample prompt sets, discussion of caching effects and production rollout guardrails. Customer concerned about clinical NLP false positives and wants deterministic regression tests and clear SLOs for tail latency.
topics: Console UI: qprofile presets and custom profile editor
INT8 v FP8: token throughput, latency, and subjective fidelity
Security: KMS integration, audit logs, VPC/private control plane
Pilot success metrics and evaluation harness
transcript: 00:00:02 Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for doing this — we're gonna run through the Optimize console and do a quick INT8 vs FP8 sandbox. If you have screen, you should see my deck + console now.
00:00:12 Priya Kapoor: Yep I see your screen. Quick ask up front — our main worry is fidelity on clinical entity extraction, so low tolerance for hallucinations.
00:00:20 Maya Chen: Totally. We'll focus on quality metrics and you can drop your gold prompts in the shared folder after. Liam will demo the live perf runs.
00:00:28 Liam O'Connor: Hey, I'm gonna start with an INT8 profile, then swap to FP8 and show the console diff — latency waterfall, token per second and a small fidelity score from the eval runner.
00:00:42 Ethan Marsh: Quick infra note — we plan to run the pilot on-prem with RDW dedicated nodes, so need the on-prem runbook for config, and KMS route for keys.
00:00:52 Sofia Alvarez: And also SOC2 evidence, plus how audit logs look when model prompts contain PHI, even if we don't store persisted copies.
00:01:03 Maya Chen: We'll share the SOC2 + KMS whitepaper after. For PHI handling we recommend on-prem control plane and customer-managed KMS, which you flagged earlier.

00:01:20 Liam O'Connor: Jumping to the console — Home > Optimize > Profiles. Here are our presets: balanced-low-latency, fidelity-prioritized, and an experimental fp8-high-fidelity. Note: console sometimes shows 'Optima' in the UI placeholder, ignore that — it's a small localization bug.
00:01:42 Liam O'Connor: First INT8 run: single request stream, 512 tokens context, 8 concurrent streams. Measured p50 ~ 22ms per token, p95 ~ 120ms per token, throughput ~ 380 tokens/s on this node.
00:02:05 Priya Kapoor: Those p95 numbers seem high, our app needs tail below 90ms for interactive clinical tagging.
00:02:12 Liam O'Connor: Right, that's where caching and batching policy matter. For prefix caching with common prompts, p95 dropped to 78ms in another run — I'll demo that after.
00:02:28 Maya Chen: Also note that INT8 generally gives lower latency and cost, but we saw fidelity regressions on a couple of sensitive prompts in our eval harness.
00:02:37 Priya Kapoor: Can you quantify 'regressions'? How are you scoring fidelity here?

00:02:44 Liam O'Connor: We use a mixed metric: exact-match on entity spans + semantic similarity threshold. In this sample, INT8 dropped exact-match by ~3.7% on the clinical set, while FP8 kept within 0.6% of baseline.
00:03:05 Ethan Marsh: Is that across 3 prompt templates or more? Our traffic shape is highly skewed to very short prompts.
00:03:11 Liam O'Connor: This run was 50 prompts (representative), mostly mid-length. If your traffic skews short, the absolute delta might differ — short prompts sometimes reduce quant-sensitivity.
00:03:26 Priya Kapoor: Short prompts are 60% of traffic, then 30% medium, 10% long. We'll upload exact mixes.
00:03:34 Maya Chen: Great. I'll note upload in next steps. Now switching to FP8 profile — hit Deploy in console.
00:03:44 [screen change sound] Liam O'Connor: FP8 run: p50 ~ 28ms/token, p95 ~ 95ms/token, throughput ~ 290 tokens/s. Fidelity delta vs baseline less than 1% on our clinical eval.
00:04:05 Priya Kapoor: So FP8 is a middle ground — slightly slower but better fidelity.
00:04:10 Liam O'Connor: Exactly. Also cost difference per token is about +18% for FP8 vs INT8 on our current pricing model for dedicated nodes.
00:04:20 Ethan Marsh: That cost delta matters — we have a tight budget for inference spend. Do you have a cost/perf workbook we can plug numbers into?
00:04:27 Maya Chen: Yes, I'll share a workbook with modeled throughput, batch sizes, and expected monthly spend based on your traffic mix. I'll include optimized batching and cache recommendations.
00:04:40 Sofia Alvarez: On the security side, how are cache keys and partial outputs handled in logs? Need to ensure no PHI leaks to Redwood logs.

00:04:49 Liam O'Connor: By default, we mask content in shared logs and we recommend customer-managed KMS and private control plane for PHI. Audit logs record metadata and hashes, not full prompts, unless you opt in.
00:05:04 Priya Kapoor: Good. Can we see an example log line?

00:05:09 Liam O'Connor: Sure — I'm switching to the trace viewer. Example: timestamp, model_id, request_id, latency_ms, cache_hit boolean, token_count. Prompt hash is salted; raw prompt is not in default logs.
00:05:26 Priya Kapoor: OK that's acceptable for now. Back to quality — can you show us the console's evaluation playback with diffs?
00:05:33 Liam O'Connor: Yep, Optimize > Evaluations > <clinical-set-1>. Here's a side-by-side diff of INT8 vs FP8 on sample 12 — INT8 merged two entities incorrectly, FP8 preserved separation.
00:05:50 Priya Kapoor: Hmm, that merge is critical — it's the difference between diagnosis A vs A+B. We can't tolerate that in production.

00:05:57 Maya Chen: Agreed. For cases like that we recommend a staged rollout: start FP8 for the clinical pipeline, run golden prompt regression daily, and enable automatic rollback if fidelity drops below threshold.
00:06:11 Ethan Marsh: Staged rollout: can you do canary by traffic percentage in the console?
00:06:15 Liam O'Connor: Yes — route 1% -> FP8 canary, monitor evals and latency. The console has a canary monitor and an automatic fallback to a pinned model/variant if errors exceed thresholds.
00:06:30 Priya Kapoor: For the backfill jobs that tag historical notes, we can run FP8 in batch mode where latency isn't critical.
00:06:36 Maya Chen: Right, use mixed-precision profiles: FP8 for online critical pipelines, INT8 for background batch to save cost.
00:06:45 [overlap] Priya Kapoor: That could work — need to see exact numbers though.

00:06:50 Liam O'Connor: I'll attach a sample spreadsheet that models cost per 1M tokens with different mixes. Also note quant-sensitive tokens: some medical abbreviations were tokenized in ways that exaggerated INT8 errors in our early tests.
00:07:07 Priya Kapoor: Any guidance on prompt engineering to reduce quant sensitivity?

00:07:11 Liam O'Connor: Yes — prefer canonicalized phrasing, fewer ambiguous abbreviations, and explicit entity separators. We also recommend small prompt-level perturbation tests as part of your evals.
00:07:25 Ethan Marsh: On autoscaling: when traffic spikes, do we see a large latency bump during scale-up with INT8 profiles?

00:07:32 Liam O'Connor: Scale-up can add ~150-300ms to first token for cold nodes depending on kernel JIT and KV cache warmup. Dedicated pools with pre-warm and burst capacity reduce that substantially.
00:07:46 Maya Chen: That's an important note — if tail latency is critical, configure a minimum pool size or use dedicated reserved capacity.
00:07:58 Priya Kapoor: We could reserve a small dedicated pool for critical endpoints and let batch jobs run on shared capacity.
00:08:03 Maya Chen: Exactly; that's a common pattern. Now I'm going to run a short stress test in the console: 200 concurrent short prompts to see p95 behaviour with and without prefix cache.

00:08:15 [pause / typing sounds] Liam O'Connor: Starting test now... INT8 no-cache: p95 150ms; INT8 with prefix cache: p95 82ms; FP8 with cache: p95 95ms. Those numbers align with earlier numbers but show cache benefits.
00:08:35 Priya Kapoor: The cache improvement is compelling — but need to understand cache invalidation for dynamic prompts.
00:08:41 Liam O'Connor: We expose TTLs and tagging for cache entries; you can evict by tag when content changes. We also have prefix-only caching to limit exposure.
00:08:55 Sofia Alvarez: What are the retention settings for cached keys and where are those stored?
00:09:00 Liam O'Connor: Cache metadata and salted hashes are stored in customer-controlled VPC for private deployments; in hosted mode we encrypt at rest and allow customer rotation via KMS.
00:09:13 Priya Kapoor: Ok. About the regression tests — how automated can that be?
00:09:18 Liam O'Connor: Fully automated: you upload golden prompts, define quality thresholds, schedule nightly runs. Console alerts if any profile falls below threshold and can trigger rollback.
00:09:31 Ethan Marsh: Timeline question — if we start pilot next week, how long to get meaningful results?
00:09:36 Maya Chen: Typical pilot: 2 weeks for functional regression + one week for perf under production-like load. So 3 weeks total to decide on FP8 vs INT8 for your critical path.
00:09:48 Priya Kapoor: That seems fine. We'll need to align security review in parallel — Sofia will sync with your security contact.
00:09:55 Sofia Alvarez: I'll do that. Also need a data flow diagram and retention policy.
00:10:01 Maya Chen: We'll attach those docs to the CRM and share a dedicated link to the architecture diagram.
00:10:09 Liam O'Connor: One more demo item: show console's model variant diff view — here's token-level diff heatmap. You can click a sample and see how logits changed between INT8 and FP8.
00:10:22 Priya Kapoor: That's helpful — gives a visual cue on where model diverges.
00:10:27 Ethan Marsh: Any notes on cluster sizing for on-prem? We're thinking 8x A100 equivalent nodes for initial pilot.
00:10:34 Liam O'Connor: 8x A100 is overkill for a small pilot; 2-4 nodes should be fine depending on concurrency. We'll run assumptions in the workbook.
00:10:45 Maya Chen: I'll send recommended node configs in the runbook. Also note GPU type impacts INT8/FP8 perf differently.
00:10:52 Priya Kapoor: Right. Anything else on gating criteria for acceptance?
00:10:56 Ethan Marsh: For us: fidelity > 99% entity match on golden set, p95 < 100ms on live traffic for critical endpoints, and no PHI leakage in logs. If those hit, move to prod.
00:11:10 Maya Chen: Noted. We'll reflect those in the pilot success metrics in the workbook.
00:11:17 [brief silence, typing] Maya Chen: Alright, to wrap — recap and next steps.

00:11:22 Maya Chen: Next steps: Maya to send perf/cost workbook and qprofiles; Liam to stand up INT8/FP8 test harness and run on-prem template; Priya to upload prompt sets; Ethan to confirm node specs; Sofia to schedule security sync. We suggest pilot start next week but flexible.
00:11:43 Priya Kapoor: Sounds good. Can you include a copy of the console export with the exact test run IDs so we can reproduce?
00:11:49 Liam O'Connor: Yes — will include run IDs and raw traces. Note some trace fields are redacted in hosted mode, but in private deployment you'll get full traces under your VPC.
00:12:02 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and runbook by Friday. Any final questions?
00:12:09 Ethan Marsh: No, thanks. Looking forward to the pilot.
00:12:13 Priya Kapoor: Thanks, bye.
00:12:15 Sofia Alvarez: Bye.
00:12:18 Maya Chen: Bye all, talk soon. [call ends]
